summary: Grant County, OR 90-ft tree lookout in Malheur NF, built 1924, staffed that season, listed abandoned with no date. Nothing describes the site today.

facts.status_note: firelookout.com and the lookout index list it as abandoned, with no date; no source says whether anything stands there today

events.note: Built by Forest Service Ranger Glover Blake, per a 1968 Sunday Oregonian item; firelookout.com records a 90-foot crow's nest for 1924
Lookout station closed for the year in September 1924 and smoke chasers relieved from duty (Burns Times-Herald, September 27, 1924); earliest staffing in the sources read

evidence.supports: location 24 miles northeast of John Day
on Myrtle Butte in the Malheur National Forest
evidence.quote: on Myrtle Butte in the Malheur National Forest

evidence.supports: 1968 Sunday Oregonian item: 90-foot tree lookout built by Forest Service Ranger Glover Blake in 1924
evidence.quote: September 1, 1968: Typical of Oregon's forest lookout stations in the old days was this 90-foot tree lookout on Myrtle Butte in the Malheur National Forest. This elongated fire lookout post was built by Forest Service Ranger Glover Blake in 1924. (Sunday Oregonian)

evidence.supports: station closed for the year, September 1924 (Burns Times-Herald)
evidence.quote: September 27, 1924: The Myrtle Butte lookout station has been closed for the year and smoke chasers have been relieved from duty. (Burns Times-Herald)

evidence.supports: index entry: Crowsnest type, Abandoned status

corrections.why: The index and firelookout.com both say abandoned, not gone. Neither says the tower was removed or destroyed.
Firelookout.com describes a 90-foot crow's nest, and the index types this site as Crowsnest.

notes_for_editor: Brief record has two errors: status should be abandoned (not gone) and kind should be crowsnest (not platform); see corrections. Both are now reflected in facts and the story. Only the 1924 season is documented for staffing. The 1968 article gives the builder's name as Glover Blake; a web search surfaced a Grover C. Blake tied to Big Butte on the Umatilla, which is unrelated and was not used. West Myrtle Butte (NHLR, standing 60-foot tower, 1929) is a different lookout and must not be merged. Access is unknown; no visit or access fact was found.
